first.rationale: Prioritize verification of promotional pricing because it is highly consequential under competitive pressure but its inherited evidence does not establish sustainable qualified revenue after discounting. Verify onboarding shortening because it directly addresses both declining completion and activation. Current intent is a guarded standard onboarding-simplification experiment, with qualification and downstream revenue monitored because reducing steps or data collection could degrade lead/account quality.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline, and the verified prior experiment improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%. Promotional pricing is rejected for this cycle: despite acquisition and qualified-revenue lift, the verified discounted cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Guard against reduced qualification/data capture by measuring downstream qualified revenue, retention, and account quality alongside activation and completion.

final2.rationale: Continue with onboarding simplification rather than reactively deploy deeper promotional pricing. The verified onboarding result directly improves the currently declining completion and activation metrics while increasing 30-day retention. The only available pricing evidence showed that a 40% targeted discount produced short-term qualified-revenue lift but materially weakened retention and did not survive first renewal, making escalation in response to the competitor inconsistent with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and downstream account quality as material risks that this experiment will not fully address.
